readings.title: First Fruits and Tithes
readings.subtitle: Acknowledging the Giver of the Land
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 26:1] “And it shall be, when you come into the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you as an inheritance, and you possess it and dwell in it, [2] that you shall take some of the first of all the produce of the ground, which you bring from your land that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, and put it in a basket and go to the place where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> chooses to make <dn>His</dn> Name dwell. [3] “And you shall come to the one who is priest in those days, and say to him, ‘I declare today to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> that I have come to the country which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> swore to our fathers to give us.’ [4] “And the priest shall take <dn>את</dn> the basket from your hand and set it down before the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [5] “And you shall answer and say before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, ‘My father was a perishing Aramean, and he went down to Mitsrayim and sojourned there with few men. And there he became a nation, great, mighty, and numerous. [6] ‘And the Mitsrites did evil to <dn>את</dn> us, and afflicted us, and imposed hard labour on us. [7] ‘Then we cried out to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of our fathers, and <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> heard <dn>את</dn> our voice and saw <dn>את</dn> our affliction and <dn>את</dn> our toil and <dn>את</dn> our oppression. [8] ‘And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brought us out of Mitsrayim with a strong hand and with an outstretched arm, and with great fear and with signs and wonders, [9] and <dn>He</dn> brought us to this place and has given us <dn>את</dn> this land, a land flowing with milk and honey. [10] ‘And now, see, I have brought <dn>את</dn> the first-fruits of the land which <dn>You</dn>, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, have given me.’ And you shall set it down before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and bow down before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, [11] and rejoice in all the good which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given to you and your house, you and the Lĕwite and the stranger who is among you. [12] “When you have completed tithing <dn>את</dn> all the tithe of your increase in the third year, which is the year of tithing, and have given it to the Lĕwite, to the stranger, to the fatherless, and to the widow, and they have eaten within your gates and have been satisfied, [13] then you shall say before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, ‘I have put away the set-apart portion from my house, and also have given it to the Lĕwite, and to the stranger, and to the fatherless, and to the widow, according to all <dn>Your</dn> command which <dn>You</dn> have commanded me. I have not transgressed <dn>Your</dn> commands, nor have I forgotten. [14] ‘I have not eaten of it when in my mourning, nor have I removed it for any unclean use, nor given any of it for the dead. I have obeyed the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> my <dn>Elohim</dn>. I have done according to all that <dn>You</dn> have commanded me. [15] ‘Look from <dn>Your</dn> set-apart dwelling place, from the heavens, and bless <dn>את</dn> <dn>Your</dn> people Yisra’el and <dn>את</dn> the land which <dn>You</dn> have given us, as <dn>You</dn> swore to our fathers, a land flowing with milk and honey.’

readings.title: A Set-Apart People
readings.subtitle: The Covenant Relationship Confirmed
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 26:16] “This day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is commanding you to do <dn>את</dn> these laws and right-rulings. And you shall guard and do them with all your heart and with all your being. [17] “You have today caused <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to proclaim to be your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and to walk in <dn>His</dn> ways and guard <dn>His</dn> laws, and <dn>His</dn> commands, and <dn>His</dn> right-rulings, and to obey <dn>His</dn> voice. [18] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has caused you to proclaim today to be <dn>His</dn> people, a treasured possession, as <dn>He</dn> has spoken to you, and to guard all <dn>His</dn> commands, [19] so as to set you high above all nations which <dn>He</dn> has made, for a praise, and for a name, and for esteem, and for you to be a set-apart people to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, as <dn>He</dn> has spoken.”

readings.title: The Stones and the Altar
readings.subtitle: Writing the Law on Mount Ebal
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 27:1] And Mosheh, with the elders of Yisra’el, commanded <dn>את</dn> the people, saying, “Guard <dn>את</dn> every command which I command you today. [2] “And it shall be, on the day when you pass over <dn>את</dn> the Yarden to the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, that you shall set up for yourselves great stones and whitewash them with lime. [3] “And you shall write on them <dn>את</dn> all the Words of this Torah, when you have passed over, so that you go into the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you, ‘a land flowing with milk and honey,’ as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of your fathers has spoken to you. [4] “And it shall be, when you have passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yarden, that on Mount Ěy,ḇal you set up <dn>את</dn> these stones, which I command you today, and you shall whitewash them with lime. [5] “And there you shall build a slaughter-place to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, a slaughter-place of stones. Do not wield an iron tool on them. [6] “Build <dn>את</dn> the slaughter-place of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> with complete stones. And you shall offer ascending offerings on it to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, [7] and shall slaughter peace offerings, and eat there, and rejoice before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [8] “And you shall write all the Words of this Torah on the stones, plainly and well.” [9] And Mosheh and the priests, the Lĕwites, spoke to all Yisra’el, saying, “Be silent and hear, O Yisra’el: This day you have become the people of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [10] “And you shall obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, and do <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> commands and <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> laws which I command you today.”

readings.title: The Curses of Ebal
readings.subtitle: Consequences for Secret Sins
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 27:11] And Mosheh commanded <dn>את</dn> the people on the same day, saying, [12] “These shall stand on Mount Gerizim to bless <dn>את</dn> the people, when you have passed over <dn>את</dn> the Yarden: Shimʽon, and Lĕwi, and Yehuḏah, and Yissasḵar, and Yosĕph, and Binyamin. [13] “And these shall stand on Mount Ěyḇal to curse: Re’uḇĕn, Gad, and Ashĕr, and Zeḇulun, Dan, and Naphtali. [14] “And the Lĕwites shall speak with a loud voice and say to all the men of Yisra’el: [15] ‘Cursed is the man who makes a carved or moulded image, an abomination to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, the work of the hands of the craftsman, and sets it up in secret.’ And all the people shall answer and say, ‘Amĕn!’ [16] ‘Cursed is he who treats his father or his mother with contempt.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’ [17] ‘Cursed is he who moves his neighbour’s boundary.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’ [18] ‘Cursed is he who misleads a blind one on the way.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’ [19] ‘Cursed is he who twists the right-ruling of the stranger, the fatherless, and widow.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’ [20] ‘Cursed is he who lies with his father’s wife, because he has uncovered his father’s skirt.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’ [21] ‘Cursed is he who lies with any beast.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’ [22] ‘Cursed is he who lies with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’ [23] ‘Cursed is he who lies with his mother-in-law.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’ [24] ‘Cursed is he who smites his neighbour secretly.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’ [25] ‘Cursed is he who takes a bribe to slay an innocent being.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’ [26] ‘Cursed is he who does not establish <dn>את</dn> the Words of this Torah, to do them.’ And all the people shall say, ‘Amĕn!’

readings.subsection: The Two Paths Set Before Israel
readings.title: The Blessings of Obedience
readings.subtitle: Fruitfulness, Victory, and Prosperity
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 28:1] “And it shall be, if you diligently obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to guard to do <dn>את</dn> all <dn>His</dn> commands which I command you today, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> shall set you high above all nations of the earth. [2] “And all these blessings shall come upon you and overtake you, if you obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>: [3] “Blessed are you in the city, and blessed are you in the field. [4] “Blessed is the fruit of your body, and the fruit of your ground and the fruit of your livestock – the increase of your cattle and the offspring of your flocks. [5] “Blessed is your basket and your kneading bowl. [6] “Blessed are you when you come in, and blessed are you when you go out. [7] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> causes your enemies who rise against you to be smitten before your face – they come out against you one way and flee before you seven ways. [8] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commands the blessing on you in your storehouses and in all to which you set your hand, and shall bless you in the land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> is giving you. [9] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> establishes you as a set-apart people to <dn>Himself</dn>, as <dn>He</dn> has sworn to you, if you guard <dn>את</dn> the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> and walk in <dn>His</dn> ways. [10] “And all peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is called upon you, and they shall be afraid of you. [11] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall make you to abound in what is good, in the fruit of your body, and in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your ground, in the land of which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> swore to your fathers to give you. [12] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> opens to you <dn>את</dn> <dn>His</dn> good treasure, the heavens, to give the rain to your land in its season, and to bless <dn>את</dn> all the work of your hand. And you shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow. [13] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall make you the head and not the tail. And you shall be only on top, and not be beneath, if you obey the commands of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, which I command you today, to guard and to do, [14] and do not turn aside from any of the Words which I command you today, right or left, to go after other mighty ones to serve them.

readings.title: Curses for Disobedience - Part 1
readings.subtitle: Sickness, Defeat, and Oppression
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 28:15] “And it shall be, if you do not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to guard to do <dn>את</dn> all <dn>His</dn> commands and <dn>His</dn> laws which I command you today, that all these curses shall come upon you and overtake you: [16] “Cursed are you in the city, and cursed are you in the field. [17] “Cursed is your basket and your kneading bowl. [18] “Cursed is the fruit of your body and the fruit of your land, the increase of your cattle and the offspring of your flocks. [19] “Cursed are you when you come in, and cursed are you when you go out. [20] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sends on you <dn>את</dn> the curse, <dn>את</dn> the confusion, and <dn>את</dn> the rebuke in all that you set your hand to do, until you are destroyed and until you perish quickly, because of the evil of your deeds by which you have forsaken <dn>Me</dn>. [21] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> makes <dn>את</dn> the plague cling to you until <dn>He</dn> has consumed you from the land which you are going to possess. [22] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> strikes you with wasting disease, and with inflammation, and with burning, and with extreme heat, and with the sword, and with blight, and with mildew. And they shall pursue you until you perish. [23] “And your heavens which are over your head shall be bronze, and the earth which is under you iron. [24] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> makes <dn>את</dn> the rain of your land powder and dust; from the heavens it comes down on you until you are destroyed. [25] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> causes you to be defeated before your enemies – you go out one way against them and flee seven ways before them. And you shall become a horror to all the reigns of the earth. [26] “And your carcasses shall be food for all the birds of the heavens and the beasts of the earth, with no one to frighten them away. [27] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> strikes you with the boils of Mitsrayim, with tumours, with the scab, and with the itch, from which you are unable to be healed. [28] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> strikes you with madness and blindness and confusion of heart. [29] “And you shall be groping at noon, as a blind man gropes in darkness, and not prosper in your ways. And you shall be only oppressed and plundered all the days, with no one to save you. [30] “You become engaged to a wife, but another man lies with her. You build a house, but do not dwell in it. You plant a vineyard, but do not use its fruit. [31] “Your ox is slaughtered before your eyes, but you do not eat of it. Your donkey is violently taken from before you, and it is not given back to you. Your sheep are given to your enemies, with no one to save you. [32] “Your sons and your daughters are given to another people, and your eyes look and fail with longing for them all day long, and your hand is powerless. [33] “A people whom you have not known eat the fruit of your land and all your labours. And you shall be only oppressed and crushed all the days. [34] “And you shall be maddened because of the sight which your eyes see. [35] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> strikes you in the knees and on the legs with evil boils of which you are unable to be healed, and from the sole of your foot to the top of your head. [36] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brings <dn>את</dn> you and <dn>את</dn> the sovereign whom you set over you to a nation which neither you nor your fathers have known, and there you shall serve other mighty ones, wood and stone. [37] “And you shall become an astonishment, a proverb, and a mockery among all peoples where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> drives you. [38] “You take much seed out into the field but gather little in, for the locust consumes it. [39] “You plant vineyards and tend them, but you neither drink of the wine nor gather the grapes, for the worm eats them. [40] “You have olive trees in all your border, but you do not anoint yourself with the oil, for your olives drop off. [41] “You bring forth sons and daughters, but they are not with you, for they go into captivity. [42] “All your trees and fruit of your land the creeping locust possesses. [43] “The stranger who is among you rises higher and higher above you, but you come down lower and lower. [44] “He lends to you, but you do not lend to him. He is the head, and you are the tail.

readings.title: Curses for Disobedience - Part 2
readings.subtitle: The Ultimate Exile and Despair
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 28:45] “And all these curses shall come upon you, and they shall pursue and overtake you, until you are destroyed, because you did not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, to guard <dn>His</dn> commands and <dn>His</dn> laws which <dn>He</dn> commanded you. [46] “And they shall be upon you for a sign and for a wonder, and on your seed forever. [47] “Because you did not serve <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> with joy and gladness of heart, for the abundance of everything, [48] therefore you shall serve <dn>את</dn> your enemies whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> sends against you, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in need of everything. And <dn>He</dn> shall put a yoke of iron on your neck until <dn>He</dn> has destroyed you. [49] “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> brings a nation against you from afar, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flies, a nation whose language you shall not understand, [50] a nation fierce of face, which does not show partiality to the elderly nor show favour to the young. [51] “And it shall eat the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your land, until you are destroyed. It leaves you no grain, nor new wine, nor oil, nor the increase of your cattle, nor the offspring of your flocks, until it has destroyed you. [52] “And it shall besiege you in all your gates until your high and fenced walls, in which you are trusting, come down in all your land. And it shall besiege you in all your gates in all your land which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given you. [53] “And you shall eat the fruit of your own body, the flesh of your sons and your daughters whom <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> has given you, in the siege and distress with which your enemies distress you. [54] “The man among you who is tender, and who is very delicate, his eye is evil against his brother, against the wife of his bosom, and against the remnant of his children whom he leaves behind, [55] against giving any of them the flesh of his children that he eats, because it is all that is left to him in the siege and distress with which your enemy distresses you in all your gates. [56] “The tender and the delicate woman among you, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot on the ground because of her delicateness and tenderness, her eye is evil against the husband of her bosom, and against her son, and against her daughter, [57] and against her afterbirth which comes out from between her feet, and against her children whom she bears, for she eats them in secret for need of everything in the siege and distress with which your enemy distresses you in your gates. [58] “If you do not guard to do <dn>את</dn> all the Words of this Torah that are written in this book, to fear <dn>את</dn> this esteemed and awesome Name, <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>, [59] then <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall make <dn>את</dn> your plagues wondrous, and <dn>את</dn> the plagues of your seed, great and lasting plagues and evil and lasting sicknesses. [60] “And <dn>He</dn> shall bring back on you <dn>את</dn> all the diseases of Mitsrayim, of which you were afraid, and they shall cling to you. [61] “Also every sickness and every plague, which is not written in the book of this Torah, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> does bring upon you until you are destroyed. [62] “And you shall be left with few men, although you had become as the stars of the heavens in number, because you did not obey the voice of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>. [63] “And it shall be, that as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> rejoiced over you to do you good and increase you, so <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> rejoices over you to destroy <dn>את</dn> you and bring <dn>את</dn> you to naught. And you shall be plucked from off the land which you go to possess. [64] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall scatter you among all peoples, from one end of the earth to the other, and there you shall serve other mighty ones, which neither you nor your fathers have known, wood and stone. [65] “And among those nations you are to find no rest, nor have a resting place for the sole of your foot. But there <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall give you a trembling heart, and failing eyes, and pining of being. [66] “And your life shall be hanging in suspense before you, and you shall fear day and night, and not believe in your life. [67] “In the morning you say, ‘Oh, that it were evening!’ And at evening you say, ‘Oh, that it were morning!’ because of the fear of your heart which you fear, and because of the sight which your eyes see. [68] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall bring you back to Mitsrayim in ships, by a way of which I said to you, ‘You are never to see it again.’ And there you shall be sold to your enemies for slaves and female slaves, and no one to buy.”

readings.title: The Covenant in Moab
readings.subtitle: A Renewal of the Oath
readings.text: [Deuteronomy 29:1] These are the words of the covenant which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh to make with <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’el in the land of Mo’aḇ, besides the covenant which <dn>He</dn> made with them in Ḥorĕḇ.
